clue.text: Transfer gathering of troops to appear acceptable

parts.note: to transfer a ball or an object to someone is to pass it
a muster is an assembly of soldiers for inspection

explanation.surface: Moving an army parade somewhere else so that it looks fit for inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass muster is an idiom for being judged good enough when examined.

clue.text: Sort of bird unfashionable outside Ire land

indicators.note: outside means the first word's letters wrap around the second

parts.note: passé means out of date or no longer in fashion
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland (printed here split as Ire land)

explanation.surface: Some kind of bird considered out of date beyond the Irish shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ire land' is how the page split 'Ireland'; 'unfashionable' looks like it describes the bird but supplies the wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: Passerines are the perching birds, the order that includes sparrows and finches.

clue.text: Bench, initially divided, came to agreement

parts.note: a settle is a long wooden bench with a high back

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word divided

explanation.surface: A bench, split at first, ends up with everyone agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled as a verb means resolved a dispute, reaching an agreed outcome.

clue.text: Upper class forcing open rebellion

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage
prising means levering something open by force

explanation.surface: The aristocracy breaking open a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular revolt against authority, a synonym of rebellion.

clue.text: One very reliable tugboat?

definitions.meaning: someone dependable who gives support in hard times
read literally, a vessel whose pulling power is great, a towing vessel of strength

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a steadfast supporter, and literally suggests a powerful towing boat.

clue.text: Percussionist losing top of denture in glass

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the percussionist's word

parts.note: a drummer is a player of percussion

indicators.note: top of picks out the first letter of denture, as this is a down clue

explanation.surface: A drummer losing a front false tooth into a drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummer is a large stemmed drinking glass, typically for wine.

clue.text: Release without charge

definitions.meaning: to let go or liberate someone

explanation.definitionFit: Free is both a verb meaning liberate and an adjective meaning costing nothing.

clue.text: A small stronghold in Wonderland?

parts.note: read whimsically as a fort belonging to the girl who went to Wonderland, it names an archaic word for a little fort

explanation.definitionFit: A fortalice is an old word for a small fort or outwork of a fortification.

clue.text: Pull out hair as English procurator

parts.note: Pontius Pilate was the Roman procurator of Judaea

explanation.surface: A Roman governor plucking out hair in the English manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To epilate is to remove hair by the roots, a technical synonym for depilating.

clue.text: Fixed wage should discourage creep

parts.note: set means fixed or established
screw is British slang for a salary or wage

explanation.surface: A settled salary ought to deter a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' looks like a toady; it is the slow slipping of a part, which this fastener stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A setscrew is a screw that holds a part in position, preventing it from slipping out of place.

clue.text: Showing unhealthy interest in higher-sounding offer

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for higher is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a higher bid is more
a bid is an offer at an auction

explanation.surface: An auction bidder takes a ghoulish interest in a bigger offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Morbid describes an abnormal fascination with death or disease.

clue.text: Girl's energy completely back

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: back means the word for completely is read in reverse

parts.note: all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: A young woman whose vigour has fully returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's name, as in Ella Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Homeless boy discovers way a bolt turns

parts.note: a street is a road or way

indicators.note: turns means the bolt and the a are read backwards together

parts.note: a bar is a bolt for fastening a door

explanation.surface: A lad finds out which way a door bolt rotates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses BAR A to give ARAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Street arab is a dated term for a homeless child living rough in a city.

clue.text: Insure my end if in distress

indicators.note: in distress signals the letters of the fodder are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arrange cover against my death if things go badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To indemnify is to protect someone against loss, which is what insuring does.

clue.text: Choose exam for this sort of college

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Picking a viva as the test for entry to a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College' suggests a university, but it is the US body that formally chooses the president.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electoral College is the body that elects the US president, so electoral describes that sort of college.

clue.text: Seedy clubs for a rich man

definitions.meaning: a dive is a disreputable bar or nightclub
The traditional name of the rich man in the parable of Lazarus

explanation.definitionFit: Dives are sleazy clubs, and Dives is the rich man of Luke's parable.

clue.text: Device to lift up large confections

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: mega means huge or large
tarts are sweet pastry confections

explanation.surface: A gadget for raising big cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift up' reverses MEGA TARTS to STRATAGEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning device or scheme to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Postponement of payment to sunbathe in the middle of Africa

indicators.note: in tells us the sunbathing word sits inside the African country

parts.note: the Congo lies in central Africa
to tan is to sunbathe

explanation.surface: Putting off a bill so you can lie in the sun deep in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of Africa' looks like a letter pick; it is a country there.
explanation.definitionFit: Contango is a Stock Exchange term for the fee paid to defer settlement of a purchase.

clue.text: Fat westerner covered up

indicators.note: covered up means the answer lies concealed within the word westerner

explanation.surface: An overweight cowboy keeps himself well wrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Esters include the glycerides that make up fats, so chemistry treats fats as esters.

clue.text: If laid on the table, one may need to use a cushion

definitions.text: If laid on the table, one may need to use a cushion

parts.words: If laid on the table, one may need to use a cushion
parts.note: the table is a baize games table with cushioned edges; a player blocked by a ball may need to bank off the cushion

explanation.definitionFit: In this cue game a player snookered must often play off a cushion to reach the ball.

clue.text: Doctor comes in to treat me when poorly: one has the measure of the vapours

definitions.text: one has the measure of the vapours

indicators.note: comes in places the doctor inside the rearranged letters
poorly means unwell, so these letters are in a bad way and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor arrives to treat me when I am ill, and diagnoses the vapours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when poorly' gives ATMETER. 'The vapours' suggests the old nervous ailment, but means water vapour evaporating.
explanation.definitionFit: An atmometer is an instrument measuring the rate of evaporation of water.

clue.text: Catherine, say, is a star in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Catherine the Great appears as a celebrity on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles only STAR to TSAR; IN and A follow as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine the Great was a Russian empress, an example of a tsar's wife or empress.

clue.text: Black top on this fruit could make you mad

indicators.note: the black letter sits on top of the fruit to make a word for mad, so taking it off leaves the fruit

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dark topping on fruit is enough to drive you crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds BANANAS (mad) from B on the fruit, so the fruit is BANANAS less B.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the pineapple, from its Latin genus name.

clue.text: End of training in America, say, for military force

indicators.note: in places the last letter of training inside the landmass

parts.note: America is an example of a continent

indicators.note: End of selects the final letter of training

explanation.surface: A soldier's training finishes in the United States, ready to join the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a body of troops contributed to a larger force.

clue.text: Pious platitudes the philosopher uttered

indicators.note: uttered tells us the philosopher's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher speaking only sanctimonious clichés.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk.

clue.text: Poles may help this Norwegian course? That's a come-down

definitions.text: Poles may help this Norwegian course? That's a come-down

parts.words: Poles may help this Norwegian course? That's a come-down
parts.note: the poles are ski sticks, not people from Poland, and the course runs downhill, a sport the Norwegians gave the world

explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a downhill slope where skiers use poles.

clue.text: Good casting though moving awkwardly

parts.note: casting a line is part of angling

explanation.surface: A fine throw of the line, though the fisherman moves clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone tall, thin and ungainly in movement.

clue.text: No church hymn —- it's spoken

indicators.note: No tells us the church letters are left out of the hymn word

parts.note: choral, a variant spelling of chorale, is a hymn tune

explanation.surface: No hymn singing in church today: it is all speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Roedean, say, needs empty room to accommodate graduate teacher

parts.note: Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: empty leaves only the first and last letters of room

explanation.surface: A girls' school needs a vacant room to house a teacher with a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a famous English girls' boarding school; 'empty' leaves RM, which takes in MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmarm is an old-fashioned word for a female teacher.
